Contamination-aware differential expression on pseudobulk counts.

Source: R/ambient_de.R
ambient_de.Rd

Contamination-aware differential expression on pseudobulk counts.

Usage

ambient_de(
  counts,
  empties = NULL,
  design,
  coef = ncol(design),
  soup = NULL,
  min_count = 10,
  naive = TRUE,
  robust = TRUE,
  joint_rho = TRUE,
  soup_design = TRUE,
  lfc = 0,
  max_ambient_frac = 0.75,
  huber_k = 2,
  robust_iter = 2,
  maxit = 50,
  tol = 1e-08
)

Arguments

counts

genes x samples pseudobulk counts of ONE cell type.

empties

list (one per sample, same order as counts columns) of genes x droplets empty-droplet matrices for the same genes; OR supply soup directly.

design

sample-level design matrix (rows = samples).

coef

column of design to test (index or name).

soup

optional precomputed soup_eb() result.

min_count

genes are tested only if their soup-removed pseudobulk passes edgeR's filterByExpr at this min.count.

naive

also run standard edgeR QL on the raw pseudobulk and report which of its hits the contamination-aware test does not support.

robust

down-weight outlier samples per gene (Huber weights on Pearson residuals, with the dispersion re-estimated under those weights). Guards against the false positives NB tests produce in large cohorts when a few samples carry extreme counts.

joint_rho

refine each sample's ambient fraction on genes that look absent from the cell type across ALL samples pooled. A single sample cannot tell a weakly expressed gene from an absent one, which biases its ambient fraction upward; the pooled test can.

soup_design

shrink each sample's soup toward the design-fitted soup (see soup_eb()) instead of the overall mean.

lfc

test against |log2 fold change| <= lfc instead of zero (as limma's TREAT). In cohorts of a hundred or more samples per group, residual biases well under 1% become statistically detectable; a small threshold such as log2(1.1) asks for effects that matter.

max_ambient_frac

genes whose counts in this cell type are, on average, more than this fraction ambient are not tested (they are listed in attribute "ambient_dominated"). Their native signal is too small for the ambient estimate's error.

huber_k

Huber tuning constant, in Pearson-residual units. The default 2 kept null genes calibrated with and without outliers in gate_ambient_de_cohort(); smaller values over-trim clean data and inflate false positives, larger ones let outliers through.

robust_iter

number of re-weighting rounds.

maxit, tol

Fisher-scoring controls.

Value

data.frame per tested gene: logFC (native-expression log2 fold change), F, PValue, FDR, ambient_frac (mean fraction of the gene's counts attributed to ambient), and when naive = TRUE naive_PValue, naive_FDR and ambient_driven (naive FDR < 0.05 but contamination-aware FDR >= 0.05). Attribute "samples": per-sample ambient fraction and library factors. Attribute "ambient_dominated": genes skipped as mostly soup.
